title: A Protocol for the Drop
premise: Ulyana Eastwick, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map and answers to no flag — discovers their long-term safe house has been listed for sale online, complete with interior photos that reveal hidden documents, a hidden room, and a dead man's face. The listing is bait, dropped by someone inside Meridian who wants Ulyana to run: either into an assassin's hands or straight to the press with proof of a decades-old inheritance scheme in which three governments laundered power through stolen identities. As Ulyana unravels the protocol behind 'the drop' — a dead-drop system designed to pass complicity from one generation of handlers to the next — they realize their own fabricated identity was manufactured as part of it. In the end, Ulyana gets the truth past the assassin, two intelligence services, and their own handler by making the drop public, burning Meridian's fiction at the cost of their own name.
about_author: B. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent eleven years in postings they still cannot name. They write thrillers from a coastal town where, they insist, nothing is ever dropped off the record.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't Empty
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. A routine burn-and-reset at Safe House Kestrel is interrupted when Ulyana finds the property listed on a real estate site — with photos showing the interior exactly as it stands, including the wall safe they alone should know about. The emotional beat is cold dread: someone has been inside their private world and photographed it like merchandise.

chapters.title: Meridian Hours
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Reporting the listing to her handler, Voss, triggers a lockdown order instead of an investigation; Meridian wants Kestrel erased from every database within six hours. Ulyana stalls, copies the listing metadata, and notices the photographer's watermark belongs to a man officially dead since 2019. Beat: first crack of doubt about whose side the institution is on.

chapters.title: A Buyer in Bratislava
chapters.summary: POV alternating Ulyana and the assassin, known only as Corvus. An anonymous cash offer on the house forces a viewing; Ulyana attends disguised as the estate agent while Corvus watches from across the street, waiting for whoever comes to collect what's in the safe. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, each aware a predator is near but not which one.

chapters.title: What the Safe Kept
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Inside the safe: a ledger of names, dates, and passport numbers — including Ulyana's own birth identity, dated years before she believes she existed. The documents sketch 'the Protocol,' a generational handoff of forged inheritances used to buy loyalty across three governments. Beat: vertigo; her identity is not hers, and never was.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana and a disgraced archivist, Ilse Brandt, whom the ledger implicates. Ilse explains how Meridian launders power through inherited fictions — dead men's estates, ghost heirs, purchased citizenships — and warns that any government learning the truth will kill to bury it rather than admit complicity. Beat: the enemy sharpens from a person into a system.

chapters.title: Corvus Closes
chapters.summary: POV Corvus. We learn Corvus was hired not to kill Ulyana but to retrieve the ledger and confirm its courier — Ulyana herself was the drop point all along, chosen because she'd never suspect her own life was the package. A failed interception in a Vienna train station leaves Corvus wounded and reassessing his employer. Beat: hunter begins doubting the hunt.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Confronted, Voss admits Meridian created Ulyana's identity as a living dead-drop: memories implanted through staged childhood records, her whole biography a container for the ledger's secrets. He offers her a new name and a clean exit if she surrenders the documents. Beat: grief and fury — the ultimate theft was her self.

chapters.title: The Drop, Reversed
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana and Corvus. Instead of running, Ulyana stages a fake handoff at Kestrel, using the real estate listing itself as the signal — inviting every watcher at once. Corvus, now convinced his employer intends to erase him too, defects mid-operation and covers her escape. Beat: alliance forged in betrayal; momentum turns.

chapters.title: Everything Must Go
chapters.summary: POV multiple, converging. At a staged estate auction of Kestrel's contents, Ulyana broadcasts the ledger to journalists, prosecutors, and the three governments simultaneously — making the truth too widely held to kill. Corvus eliminates the Meridian fixer sent for them both; Voss chooses institutional survival over murder and lets it happen. Beat: climax, chaos resolving into exposure.

chapters.title: Sold, Vacant Possession
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana, months later. Meridian is dismantled quietly, its principals retired rather than tried — power corrupts even justice — but the Protocol is dead. Ulyana, nameless by choice, keeps a go-bag packed out of habit, then finally unpacks it, buying a small house under a name that is genuinely hers. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity reclaimed, not restored.
